response.content:
I've reviewed the code and found several real defects.

ISSUE: line 7 | The loop condition `while d < end:` excludes the end date, contradicting the docstring which states "from start to end, inclusive". This causes the generator to miss the final date in the range.
ISSUE: line 47 | Integer division `d.month // 3 + 1` incorrectly assigns March, June, September, and December to the wrong quarter. For example, March (month 3) yields Q2 instead of Q1, and December (month 12) yields Q5 (invalid). The correct formula is `(d.month - 1) // 3 + 1`.
ISSUE: line 18 | The expression `d.month - 1 + months` can yield a negative value when subtracting more months than the current month (e.g., adding -13 months to January). In Python, `-1 // 12` is -1 and `-1 % 12` is 11, so this accidentally yields the correct date, but only by relying on implementation-specific floor division behavior that differs from most languages. If `months` is negative enough to make `month_index < -12`, the year calculation becomes incorrect for dates early in the year.
